newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says not behind rocket attack on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says not behind rocket attack on Israel.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah said on Friday it was not behind Katyusha rocket attacks on northern Israel which slightly injured a woman and damaged a synagogue.
"Hizbollah was not responsible for the rocket attacks on northern Israel today (Friday)," a Hizbollah spokesman said.
Katyusha rockets fired by guerrillas in Lebanon slammed into a northern Israeli town early on Friday, the Israeli military said.

Residents said it was the first time the rockets had landed in Kiryat Shmona, the largest town in Israel's Upper Galilee, in the more than 15 months since Israel and Hizbollah guerrillas undertook not to fire on civilian targets.
Israeli soldiers later ordered residents into bomb shelters and security rooms to guard against another possible attack on the town of 22,000 people.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility. Hizbollah (Party of God) threatened earlier this week to carry out suicide bombings inside Israel.
Cross-border violence has intensified in recent days. On Thursday five Lebanese were killed by two bombs and Israeli shelling.
Since Monday 13 people have died in the bloodshed, including seven civilians, starting with an Israeli commando raid in which five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed with a roadside bomb.
Hizbollah is fighting to drive the Israelis and their local Lebanese militia allies from Israel's 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone in south Lebanon.
Israel set up the zone -- a site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and bombs -- to protect its northern settlements from guerrilla attacks.

Israel and Hizbollah reached an understanding not to attack civilian targets as part of a 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people, mainly Lebanese civilians, were killed.
